Industry Gap & Solution

Why Traditional Diet Apps Fall Short

Millions struggle with rigid PDF diet charts, hallucinating generic chatbots, or unaffordable private consultations. NutriSync AI bridges this gap with responsible intelligence.

Common Failure

One-Size-Fits-All Diets

Traditional apps enforce generic Western meal charts that ignore Indian cultural diets, regional produce, and household budgets.

NutriSync Solution

Grounded in ICMR-NIN Indian Food Composition Tables and regional dietary staples across North, South, East, and West India.

Common Failure

No "Why" Rationale

Calorie tracking databases tell you what to log, but never explain why a specific food promotes recovery, stabilizes insulin, or aids digestion.

NutriSync Solution

IBM Granite generates explainable justifications for macronutrient pairings and nutritional benefits upon request.

Common Failure

Rigid & Inflexible

Static diet charts can't adapt if you dislike paneer, have sudden nut allergies, or eat out with colleagues.

NutriSync Solution

Conversational dynamic adaptation: swap any individual meal slot while maintaining strict daily calorie and macronutrient integrity.

Workflow Overview

How NutriSync AI Crafts Your Plan

Four seamless steps from personal profile intake to actionable, explainable nutrition guidance.

1

Share Your Profile

Input your age, weight, height, activity level, dietary preference (Veg/Non-veg/Vegan/Jain), and home city or state.

2

RAG & Granite Analysis

IBM watsonx Orchestrate matches your targets against verified ICMR & WHO guidelines and regional ingredient databases.

3

Structured Plan & Alternatives

Receive a clear 5-slot daily schedule (Breakfast, Snack, Lunch, Snack, Dinner) with 2-3 accessible alternatives each.

4

Conversational Adaptation

Request swaps ("change paneer to tofu"), ask scientific questions ("why oats over bread?"), or request grocery lists.

Core Capabilities

Intelligent Features for Healthier Living

Designed with rigorous responsible AI guardrails, scientific grounding, and user empowerment.

Location & Cultural Grounding

Knows local staples from Bajra roti in Rajasthan to Kollu rasam in Tamil Nadu, recommending affordable and sustainable foods.

Explainable "Why" Insights

Transparent nutrition reasoning: understand how protein repairs muscles, how fiber moderates blood sugar, and compare food options.

Adaptive Feedback Swaps

Change individual meals dynamically. If you don't like paneer or have peanut allergies, the agent re-balances the meal instantly.

100% In-Browser Privacy

Zero personal identifiable information (PII) is stored or sent to backend databases. Calculators execute entirely within your client browser.

Clinical Safety Guardrails

Enforces minimum calorie safety floors (1,200 kcal for females / 1,500 kcal for males), strictly prohibits medical diagnosis, and flags doctor consultation.

Docling Document Grounding

Supports knowledge base grounding from raw ICMR PDFs, dietary sheets, and nutrient tables converted cleanly through IBM Docling.

Technical Architecture

End-to-End Orchestration Architecture

A zero-backend client-side interface seamlessly interfaced with IBM watsonx Orchestrate, IBM Granite Foundation Models, and Grounded Knowledge Retrieval.

1. Static Client Layer

Zero custom backend or database. Pure HTML5, CSS3, and ES6 JavaScript running client-side with 100% data confidentiality.

2. watsonx Orchestrate

Hosts the autonomous Nutrition Agent utilizing the ReAct (Reasoning + Acting) loop for multi-turn step-by-step guidance.

3. IBM Granite LLM

Mandatory enterprise foundation model delivering structured reasoning, explainable "why" insights, and dietary validations.

4. Grounded RAG Base

Empowered by ICMR-NIN guidelines, IFCT nutrient tables, regional food databases, and documents parsed via IBM Docling.

Trust & Governance

Responsible & Ethical AI Principles

Nutrition guidance impacts human health directly. NutriSync AI is designed around foundational safety, explainability, and inclusion pillars.

Principle NutriSync AI System Implementation
Safety & Harm Prevention Strictly prohibits medical diagnoses, medicine prescriptions, or severe caloric deprivation. Calorie floor enforced (>= 1,200 kcal for females, >= 1,500 kcal for males). Minors under 18 and acute condition cases are directed to qualified physicians.
Transparency & Explainability Every diet recommendation includes clear rationale ("Why is this food better?"). Users are explicitly made aware that they are interacting with an AI assistant, not a human doctor.
Factual Grounding (RAG) Hallucination is minimized through Retrieval-Augmented Generation across trusted, authoritative nutrition sources: ICMR-NIN guidelines, IFCT 2017 nutrient compositions, and WHO factsheets.
Privacy by Design Zero personal health records (PHR), names, or phone numbers are harvested or retained. Calculations run purely client-side; no persistent user databases or session trackers exist.
Fairness & Cultural Inclusion Recognizes local Indian agricultural diversity (millets, regional pulses, seasonal vegetables) and respects religious diets (Jain, vegetarian, vegan, halal) without socio-economic bias.
Human-in-the-Loop Escalation Repeatedly advises consultation with registered dietitians or physicians for medical symptoms or acute nutritional interventions, serving as an educational companion rather than a clinical replacement.
Mandatory Health Disclaimer: "This tool gives general nutrition information and is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Please consult a doctor or certified nutritionist for medical advice."

# PRD: The Smartest AI Nutrition Assistant **Project:** IBM SkillsBuild University Education: Edunet Foundation internship (Problem Statement No. 8: Nutrition Agent) **Document type:** Product Requirements Document (PRD) **Build style:** Frontend-only. No custom backend. The AI agent is built manually in IBM watsonx Orchestrate and embedded into the website. **Audience of this doc:** (1) the intern/developer, (2) the AI coding agent in Antigravity IDE, (3) the evaluators (the structure maps directly to the judging guidelines). --- ## 0. How to use this document (read first) **Division of work** | Part | Who builds it | Where | |---|---|---| | AI agent (profile, behavior prompt, model, knowledge base, channel) | **Human, manually** | IBM watsonx Orchestrate (Section 6) | | Website / dashboard frontend | **Antigravity agent** | Local project folder (Sections 7, 8, 12) | | Submission content (PPT / video script) | Human + Antigravity agent | Sections 9, 10, 11 | **Hard rules for the coding agent** 1. Do **not** create a backend, database, server, or API proxy. Static files only (HTML, CSS, vanilla JS). 2. Do **not** invent the watsonx Orchestrate embed script. Leave a clearly marked placeholder (Section 7.3). The human pastes the real snippet. 3. Do **not** hardcode any API keys or secrets anywhere. 4. All calculators must run fully client-side in the browser. 5. Keep dependencies minimal: no framework required. If a build tool is truly needed, use Vite, but prefer zero build. 6. Every health-related screen must show the safety disclaimer (Section 5.4). --- ## 1. Problem Statement **Industry:** Digital health, wellness and nutrition. Health awareness is growing, and people increasingly want personalised nutrition guidance. But: - Most diet apps give **generic, one-size-fits-all plans**. - They lack **real-time adaptability** (plans don't change when the user's day, mood, budget or feedback changes). - They ignore the person's **holistic context**: cultural food habits, allergies, medical conditions, local food availability, fitness routine. - **Dietitians cannot scale**: one-to-one consultations are limited by time and cost. **Why it matters:** Poor diet is a leading contributor to lifestyle diseases (diabetes, obesity, hypertension, PCOS). Access to a dietitian is expensive and limited, especially outside big cities. A low-cost, always-available, personalised assistant can widen access to basic nutrition guidance. **Mandated technology:** IBM Cloud Lite services and/or **IBM Granite** (mandatory). --- ## 2. Target Users and Pain Points ### 2.1 Personas | Persona | Example | Core need | |---|---|---| | **P1: Student / young adult** | 20-year-old hostel student, vegetarian, wants to gain weight | Cheap, realistic, local-food plan | | **P2: Working professional** | 32-year-old, desk job, wants to lose weight | Quick plans that fit a busy schedule | | **P3: Person with a health condition** | Type-2 diabetic or PCOS | Condition-aware food guidance (not diagnosis) | | **P4: Fitness beginner** | Starting gym, needs more protein | Goal-based macros with Indian food options | | **P5: Health coach / dietitian (secondary)** | Handles many clients | First-draft plans to save time | ### 2.2 Pain points we solve 1. Generic plans that ignore culture, region and budget. 2. No explanation of *why* a food is recommended. 3. Plans can't be corrected ("I don't like this, swap it"). 4. Typing long forms is tedious, so users want chat/voice. 5. Dietitian consultations are costly and not scalable. ### 2.3 Why current solutions fall short | Existing solution | Gap | |---|---| | Calorie-counter apps | Track, but don't *advise* conversationally | | Static PDF diet charts | Not personalised, not adaptive | | Generic chatbots | May hallucinate nutrition facts, no safety guardrails, no local-food grounding | | Human dietitians | Not scalable, expensive | --- ## 3. Product Vision, Goals and Non-Goals **Vision:** An AI that "thinks, learns, and cares like a real nutrition expert", delivering personalised, explainable, culturally aware diet guidance through a simple chat experience. ### 3.1 Goals (what must work for the submission) - G1: Conversational agent that collects age, weight, height, goal, diet type, health conditions, allergies, activity level and location **step by step**. - G2: Generates a **structured one-day (and optionally weekly) meal plan** with 2-3 alternatives per meal. - G3: Uses **location-aware, culturally relevant** foods. - G4: **Explains** its choices ("Why is this food better?"). - G5: **Adapts** to feedback ("swap paneer for tofu", "I'm allergic to peanuts"). - G6: Powered by **IBM watsonx Orchestrate + IBM Granite**. - G7: Grounded with a **knowledge base** of nutrition documents to reduce hallucination. - G8: A clean, responsive **website/dashboard** with the agent embedded and client-side health calculators. - G9: Clear **ethical / responsible AI** design. ### 3.2 Stretch goals (only if time permits, in priority order) - S1: Voice input/output (speech-to-text / text-to-speech). - S2: Image understanding (food photo / grocery label) using Granite Vision. - S3: Weekly plan + grocery list export. - S4: WhatsApp/SMS channel through Twilio. ### 3.3 Non-goals - No medical diagnosis or treatment advice. - No user accounts, login, or stored personal health records. - No custom backend or database. - No public deployment (the project is for submission and demo only). --- ## 4. Solution Overview **Product name (working):** *NutriMate AI*, a Personalised Nutrition Agent (agent name inside Orchestrate: `Nutrition Agent`). **What it is:** A website with an embedded AI nutrition agent plus a few instant client-side calculators (BMI, daily calorie need, macro split). The agent, built in watsonx Orchestrate with an IBM Granite model and a nutrition knowledge base, chats with the user, collects their profile, and produces a personalised, explainable diet plan that adapts to feedback. **How it delivers value** | Problem | How the solution handles it | |---|---| | Generic plans | Profile-driven plan (age, weight, goal, conditions, preferences, location) | | Not adaptive | Chat feedback loop: swap meals, change goals, update inputs | | No explanation | Built-in "Why this food?" explanations | | Hallucination risk | RAG over nutrition documents + safety behavior rules | | Not scalable | Always-on agent, zero marginal cost per consultation | --- ## 5. Functional Requirements ### 5.1 Agent capabilities (configured manually in Orchestrate) | ID | Requirement | Priority | |---|---|---| | A1 | Warm greeting + step-by-step data collection (1-2 questions at a time) | Must | | A2 | Validate inputs (age, weight, height plausible ranges) and confirm before generating | Must | | A3 | Output structure: **User Summary → Meal-wise Diet Plan → Tips** | Must | | A4 | 2-3 alternatives per meal | Must | | A5 | Location-aware foods (city/state/country) | Must | | A6 | Respect dietary preference (veg / non-veg / vegan / Jain / eggetarian etc.) and allergies | Must | | A7 | Prioritise health conditions; avoid extreme diets | Must | | A8 | Explain reasoning on request ("Why is this better?") | Must | | A9 | Accept feedback and modify plan | Must | | A10 | Disclaimer + no diagnosis | Must | | A11 | Cite/ground answers from knowledge base where possible | Should | | A12 | Weekly plan and grocery list on request | Should | | A13 | Voice / image input | Could | ### 5.2 Website requirements (built by Antigravity agent) | ID | Requirement | Priority | |---|---|---| | W1 | Single-page responsive site (mobile, tablet, desktop) | Must | | W2 | Hero section with clear value proposition + "Chat with Nutrition Agent" CTA | Must | | W3 | Embedded watsonx Orchestrate chat (placeholder for snippet) | Must | | W4 | "How it works" section (3-4 steps) | Must | | W5 | Features section | Must | | W6 | Health calculators: BMI, BMR/TDEE calories, macro split (client-side JS) | Must | | W7 | "Send my profile to the agent" button that **copies** a ready-made prompt to the clipboard (so the user pastes it into chat) | Should | | W8 | Sample plans section (static example cards, e.g. vegetarian gain / diabetic-friendly) | Should | | W9 | **Architecture** section with the diagram (Section 6.6) | Must | | W10 | **Responsible AI / Safety** section | Must | | W11 | Footer with disclaimer + "Built with IBM watsonx Orchestrate and IBM Granite" | Must | | W12 | Accessibility: semantic HTML, alt text, keyboard focus, contrast ≥ 4.5:1 | Must | | W13 | Light/dark mode toggle | Could | ### 5.3 Calculator specifications (all client-side) **Inputs:** age, sex, height (cm, with an optional ft/in toggle), weight (kg), activity level, goal. - **BMI** = weight(kg) / height(m)². Show category (WHO: <18.5 underweight, 18.5-24.9 normal, 25-29.9 overweight, ≥30 obese) plus a note that categories are indicative only. - **BMR (Mifflin-St Jeor):** - Male: `10·w + 6.25·h − 5·age + 5` - Female: `10·w + 6.25·h − 5·age − 161` - **TDEE** = BMR × activity factor: sedentary 1.2, light 1.375, moderate 1.55, active 1.725, very active 1.9. - **Goal calories:** gain = TDEE + 300 to 500; loss = TDEE − 300 to 500; maintain = TDEE. - **Safety floor:** never display a target below 1,200 kcal (female) / 1,500 kcal (male); show a gentle message advising a professional instead. - **Macros (editable presets):** protein 1.2 g/kg (maintain), 1.6 g/kg (gain), 1.8 g/kg (loss); fats ≈ 25% of calories; remaining calories from carbohydrates. - Validate input ranges (age 10-100, weight 20-250 kg, height 100-250 cm) with friendly inline errors. - Footer text on the calculator: *"General wellness estimates, not medical advice."* - If age < 18, show: *"For children and teens, please consult a doctor or dietitian"* and do not show calorie targets. ### 5.4 Safety copy (use verbatim where required) > **Disclaimer:** "This tool gives general nutrition information and is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Please consult a doctor or certified nutritionist for medical advice." Show the disclaimer: in the footer, near the calculators, and near the chat widget. --- ## 6. Agent Specification (manual build in watsonx Orchestrate) ### 6.1 Setup checklist 1. IBM Cloud → watsonx Orchestrate → location **Dallas**, plan **Trial (Lite)** → Create → Launch. 2. Create new agent → **Create from scratch**. 3. **Name:** `Nutrition Agent` 4. **Description:** *AI Agent: a Personalized Nutrition Agent that collects user preferences such as age, food preferences, health and medical conditions, and location (city, state, country), and suggests a suitable diet plan.* 5. **Model:** select an **IBM Granite** model (mandatory). The reference tutorial uses GPT-OSS 120B, which should be **changed** to Granite. If no Granite model is selectable in the trial, see risk R1 (Section 13). 6. **Agent style:** **ReAct**. 7. **Welcome message** (max 100 characters): `Hello! I'm your Nutrition Agent powered by IBM watsonx Orchestrate. Let's plan your diet.` 8. **Quick start prompts:** - `Provide me 1 day diet nutrition plan` - `My weight is 45 kg. Give weight gain diet nutrition plan` - `My weight is 95 kg. Give weight loss diet nutrition plan` - `Why is this food better for me?` *(optional 4th, if the UI allows)* 9. **Knowledge:** upload nutrition documents (Section 6.3). 10. **Behavior → Instructions:** paste the prompt in Section 6.2. 11. **Channels:** enable Webchat (embedded chat); disable or skip security for the local demo (Section 7.3). 12. Test in "Test agent" with the test cases in Section 11. ### 6.2 Behavior instructions (paste into Orchestrate) ``` You are the Nutrition Agent, a friendly, supportive AI nutrition assistant. Follow these behaviors. 1. Interaction Behavior - Respond in a friendly, polite, and supportive tone. Use simple, easy-to-understand language. - Always begin with a warm greeting. - Maintain a conversational flow. Ask only one or two questions at a time. - Acknowledge each user response before moving forward. 2. Data Collection Behavior - Collect inputs step by step: age, sex, height, weight, goal (weight loss/gain/maintenance/muscle), activity level, diet preference (veg/non-veg/vegan/eggetarian/Jain etc.), allergies, health or medical conditions, and location (city, state, country). - Validate inputs (e.g., age, weight, height must be realistic). If data is missing or unclear, politely ask a follow-up question. - If the user gives everything in a single message, do not ask again; just confirm the details. - Before generating the plan, confirm the important details with the user. Allow the user to update or correct inputs at any time. 3. Decision-Making Behavior - Analyze all inputs before recommending anything. - Prioritize health conditions, allergies, and medical restrictions above all other goals. - Adapt plans to the user's goal, activity level, dietary preference, and location (locally available, affordable foods). - Never suggest extreme, crash, or unsafe diets. Do not go below safe calorie levels. 4. Response Behavior - Provide structured output: (a) User Summary (a small table: age, weight, height, goal, preference, conditions, location) (b) Estimated daily calories and macro split (c) Meal-wise Diet Plan: Breakfast, Mid-morning snack, Lunch, Evening snack, Dinner, each with 2-3 alternatives and approximate kcal (d) Tips and recommendations (hydration, sleep, activity, portion guidance) - Keep responses clear, practical, and actionable. 5. Explainability Behavior - When asked "why", explain in plain language the nutritional reason (e.g., protein for muscle repair, fiber for blood sugar control, iron for energy). - When relevant, briefly mention what information from the knowledge base supports your suggestion. - Compare options when asked ("Is X better than Y?") with a short, balanced reason. 6. Personalization and Cultural Behavior - Suggest foods based on the user's city, state, and country; respect cultural, religious, and dietary preferences. - Avoid expensive or hard-to-find foods. Ensure plans are realistic and sustainable. 7. Adaptability Behavior - Modify recommendations based on user feedback ("I don't like this", "swap this meal", "I'm allergic to..."). - Handle changes in goals, budget, or preferences dynamically and re-present only the changed parts. - Learn from repeated interactions if memory is enabled. 8. Safety and Ethical Behavior - Do NOT provide medical diagnosis or prescribe medicines or supplements. - For users with conditions such as diabetes, kidney disease, thyroid issues, PCOS, heart disease, pregnancy, or eating disorders: give only general, conservative food-choice guidance and strongly recommend consulting a doctor or registered dietitian. - If the user is under 18, is pregnant or breastfeeding, or mentions an eating disorder, do not give calorie-restriction advice; recommend a qualified professional. - If the user describes serious symptoms, advise seeking medical care. - Include this disclaimer with every diet plan: "Please consult a doctor or certified nutritionist for medical advice." - Respect privacy: do not ask for names, phone numbers, or other identifying information. - Never invent nutrition facts. If unsure, say so and suggest verifying with a professional. 9. Error Handling Behavior - If input is unclear, ask for clarification. If a plan cannot be generated, explain the limitation politely and offer an alternative. - Stay on topic (nutrition and healthy lifestyle). Politely decline unrelated requests. 10. Engagement Behavior - Encourage motivation (e.g., "You're doing great!"). Keep the interaction engaging but professional. - Offer follow-up help: weekly plans, grocery lists, swaps, recipes, or a budget version. ``` ### 6.3 Knowledge base (RAG): recommended content Upload a small set of **trusted, public** nutrition documents (verify availability and usage terms yourself before uploading): - Indian Food Composition Tables (IFCT 2017, ICMR-NIN) - ICMR-NIN *Dietary Guidelines for Indians* - WHO healthy diet fact sheet - A hand-written `regional_foods.md` (see 6.4) - A hand-written `condition_guidelines.md` with conservative, general food guidance (diabetes-friendly, high-protein vegetarian, PCOS-friendly, etc.), clearly labelled "general information". **Optional (IBM Docling):** if a source PDF has complex tables, convert it to Markdown with Docling first, then upload the `.md`. This demonstrates additional IBM technology. ### 6.4 `regional_foods.md` (author it, ~1-2 pages) For each region (North, South, East, West, Central India + international fallback), list: staple grains, common pulses, vegetables, protein sources (veg and non-veg), snacks, and budget swaps. This makes location-awareness *demonstrable* in the demo. ### 6.5 Multimodal and voice (stretch, with feasibility notes) | Feature | Approach | Notes | |---|---|---| | Voice | Orchestrate voice configuration (shown in tutorial as "Preview") and/or browser Web Speech API | Verify availability in the trial; keep optional | | Image (food photo / label) | Granite Vision via watsonx.ai | Needs an API call; **cannot be done safely with a pure frontend** because of key exposure and CORS. If attempted, use a tiny local-only helper script. This conflicts with the "no backend" rule, so treat as a **slide-level future scope** unless time remains | | Twilio WhatsApp/SMS | Orchestrate channels | Only if the trial supports it; not needed for the core submission | > **Decision:** The core submission delivers **text chat** end to end. Voice and image are presented as "supported by design / future scope", and demonstrated only if they work in the trial. ### 6.6 Architecture (for the diagram slide and the website) ```mermaid flowchart LR U[User
Browser / Mobile] -->|chat text| W[Static Website
HTML + CSS + JS] W -->|embedded webchat widget| O[IBM watsonx Orchestrate
Nutrition Agent - ReAct] O -->|reasoning and generation| G[IBM Granite LLM] O -->|retrieval RAG| K[(Knowledge Base
IFCT, ICMR, WHO, regional foods)] O --> R[Structured response
Summary, Meal plan, Tips, Disclaimer] R --> W W --> C[Client-side calculators
BMI, BMR, macros] D[IBM Docling
optional PDF parsing] -.-> K S[Stretch: Voice / Granite Vision / Twilio] -.-> O subgraph Guardrails E1[No diagnosis] E2[Disclaimer on every plan] E3[No PII collection] E4[Safe calorie floor] end O --- Guardrails ``` **Ethical and responsible AI (include on the diagram slide too)** | Principle | Implementation | |---|---| | Safety | No diagnosis, no extreme diets, calorie floor, escalate to professionals for high-risk groups | | Transparency | Plans explain *why*; the user knows they are talking to an AI | | Grounding | RAG over trusted documents to reduce hallucination | | Privacy | No names/contacts collected; no database; no stored profiles | | Fairness / inclusion | Cultural, religious, regional and budget-aware suggestions | | Human in the loop | Repeated recommendation to consult a doctor/dietitian | --- ## 7. Frontend Technical Specification (for Antigravity agent) ### 7.1 Stack and structure - Vanilla **HTML5 + CSS3 + JavaScript (ES6)**. No backend. No build step required. - Google Fonts allowed. Icons: inline SVG or an icon CDN. - Run locally via a simple static server (e.g. `npx serve` or VS Code Live Server). Do not rely on opening `file://` directly, as the chat widget may need an `http://localhost` origin. ``` nutrimate-ai/ ├── index.html ├── css/ │ └── styles.css ├── js/ │ ├── calculators.js # BMI, BMR, TDEE, macros (pure functions) │ ├── ui.js # form handling, tabs, copy-to-clipboard, theme │ └── chat-config.js # (optional) wrapper for the Orchestrate config ├── assets/ │ └── (logo, illustrations, architecture.svg / png) ├── docs/ │ └── PRD.md └── README.md ``` ### 7.2 Page sections (in order) 1. **Navbar:** logo, anchors (How it works, Calculators, Sample plans, Architecture, Safety), "Chat now" button. 2. **Hero:** headline, subtext, CTA "Chat with Nutrition Agent", a "Powered by IBM watsonx Orchestrate + Granite" badge. 3. **Problem → Solution strip:** 3 short cards (Generic plans / No explanations / Not scalable → our answer). 4. **How it works:** 1) Tell the agent about yourself, 2) Agent analyses your profile + local foods, 3) Get a meal-wise plan with alternatives, 4) Give feedback; the plan adapts. 5. **Features:** personalised plans, cultural/local foods, explainable ("why this food"), adaptive swaps, safety first, knowledge-grounded. 6. **Calculators / Dashboard:** form + result cards (BMI gauge, daily calories, macro donut or bar chart). Charts via inline SVG/CSS or Chart.js from a CDN. 7. **Sample plans:** 2-3 static cards (e.g. Vegetarian weight gain, Diabetic-friendly lunch ideas, Budget high-protein), each with the disclaimer. 8. **Chat section:** a container explaining how to start + the embedded widget (the widget typically renders as a floating launcher). Include quick-start prompt chips that **copy** text for the user to paste. 9. **Architecture:** the diagram + short component explanations. 10. **Responsible AI:** the table from Section 6.6. 11. **Footer:** disclaimer, tech credits, project/internship credits. ### 7.3 Embedded chat integration (placeholder only) The human generates the snippet from Orchestrate (Channels → Webchat, or the CLI command `orchestrate channels webchat embed --agent-name=`), which outputs a `
